Commentary.Commentary: New Zealand will be trying to chase this down after two unsuccessful attempts in this ODI series. A good opening partnership might help them to get a consolation win to wrap up the series on a winning note. Join us back up in a quick while for the run chase.

Excellent comeback by the Aussies after a dismal start. David Warner led their batting attack with some wonderful strokes. He was supported really well by Head when the Aussies were found wanting. They put up a 105-run partnership to stable the ship when they were down for 73-4 in less than 20 overs. The Kiwis could not capitalise at that very moment and they had to be satisfied with their bowling in the death overs which reduced the Aussies for less than 270. However, David Warner was brilliant. The southpaw was at his best and smashed 156 off 128 balls.

OUT! Warner is run out off the final delivery and fails to carry his bat. Fuller in length, Warner jams it to the off side and sets off. Boult goes to his right, collects the ball and scores a superb direct hit at the non-striker's end where Warner fails to make it in. What a tremendous knock though by David Warner. One of the best surely as his team was in real trouble. Australia finish on 264/8!

FOUR! What a way to reach his boundary. Warner gets his 11th hundred with a delicate glance through the on side behind the stumps. That was a beauty! It has been a brilliant year for Warner where he has racked up 7 hundreds in a calendar year, most by a player in 2016. In fact only Sachin Tendulkar has more tons in a calendar year. Such a composed knock when wickets were tickling down in the opposite end.
